content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Overestimates in late forecast period (last 5–10 days) when true values show mean reversion or downward correction.
- Tends to overshoot after recent price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 75+ forecast then true settles at 70–72).
- Underestimates when historical mean is high (e.g., 70+ range) and overestimates when historical mean is low (e.g., 60–65 range).
- Shows lag in adjusting to recent downward trends — delays correction by 2–5 days.
- Sensitive to recent volatility: if last 5 days show high variance, model overreacts with exaggerated upward bias.
- Fails to capture “rebound” after sharp drops — often underestimates recovery phase.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum — fails to account for mean reversion in 10–15 day windows.
